best_direction.angle_title: When the student changed how the work could move
best_direction.core_claim: Do not start with the accomplishment. Start at the moment the student recognized something was wrong and changed course — and stay close to what happened next. The strongest evidence sits in I have rough ideas around my sister's death, war and medicine, which keeps the direction anchored to the student's actual material instead of a reusable summary.
best_direction.why_this_is_the_real_story: Most of what led up to the correction is context. The essay is the correction itself — and the one moment after it that shows the change was real. The key turn is visible in The tension is between what happened and what it actually changed in you. That keeps the essay on the lived hinge, instead of retelling background or broad traits.
best_direction.what_it_reveals_about_the_student: It shows a student who can identify where they got it wrong and demonstrate that the correction held. The before-and-after movement is from "Operating from the obvious first version of the situation" to "Working from a more specific and accountable understanding of what," and the consequence shows up in I have rough ideas around my sister's death, war and medicine.
best_direction.why_it_beats_the_obvious_angle: A generic framing (general leadership/growth framing) would flatten the story. The evidence points to I have rough ideas around my sister's death, war, which is more specific, more draftable, and easier to trust on first read.
best_direction.main_risk_if_written_poorly: If the draft only praises initiative, it will lose the operational shift that made the work move differently.
best_direction.next_move: Open on I have rough ideas around my sister's death, war and medicine. Then show how the student changed the flow of work in I have rough ideas around my sister's death, war and medicine. Keep the essay on judgment and initiative, not self-congratulation.
